messages:
inc-bot: [ALERT] GPU_POOL_EXHAUSTION detected in us-west-2 / gpu-pool-3. queue_length=984 (warn=400, crit=800). Autoscaler attempted scale_up -> failed with provider quota errors. Severity: P1. Runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/gpu-exhaustion

Maya: ack. I'm oncall. Jumping in to triage. Starting timeline and impact notes.

Kasey: @Maya thanks — can you confirm affected routes and whether any customers are getting 5xx/429s? I'll open a bridge if this looks like multi-team. :rotating_light:

Maya: Impacted routes: /v1/generate (large), /v1/chat (high-priority). Observed symptoms: surging queue latency, clients seeing timeouts and occasional 429s from ingress when the request queue backs up. No data leak.

Derek: grabbing autoscaler logs now. Preliminary: scale_controller tried to add 8 GPUs at 2026-03-14T21:09:41Z but cloud API returned QuotaExceeded. Also noticed max_replicas was set to 30 per-pool; current pool already at 30. Looks like an earlier rollout reduced the global ceiling.

Evan: I can hotpatch the controller to bump pool max_replicas to 40 and raise scale_rate temporarily, but that requires a quick deploy (2-3m) and a restart of the scale loop. Risk: short blip in metrics while pods come up. Would reduce queued jobs by allowing more instances to be provisioned (assuming provider quota isn't the limiting factor).

Priya: Customer impact: we have 6 paying customers with >5% error rate and 12 customers with increased latency above SLO. Noting Support has opened a few tickets already.

Alex: Opening bridge now — https://meet.prod/bridge/1798765432 (bridge created). Who is taking bridge control?

Maya: I'm on bridge. Derek, can you paste the failing error snippet from the autoscaler?

Derek: paste below:
```
error: scale_up failed: QuotaExceeded: requested 5 GPUs, quota remaining 2
caller: cloudprovider/compute.go:78
controller: scale_controller.go:312
```

Kasey: Two parallel mitigations: 1) fast path: reduce incoming pressure (throttles, fallback models) so queue stops growing; 2) slow path: increase capacity (hotpatch controller + request quota increase from cloud).

Evan: I can push the hotpatch to increase pool.max_replicas to 40 and scale_rate from 1.2 -> 2.0 for 30m. I'll do a guarded rollout to canary 1 zone then roll. Requesting deploy approval.

Maya: Meanwhile: priority mitigation steps I already triggered:
- Enabled low-priority shedding: any request tagged low-priority is immediately rejected with 429 to cut incoming load.
- Enabled model-fallback routing for non-critical tenants: route to quantized-small variants to halve GPU memory and accept more concurrency.
- Lowered per-tenant concurrency limits from 10 -> 6.
These should slow queue growth in ~30s.

Priya: Support update drafted: "We are currently experiencing an autoscaling-related capacity issue in us-west-2 impacting a subset of generation requests. Teams are mitigating and we expect partial restoration in 15-30m. We will follow up with a timeline and postmortem." Approving send.

Alex: Cloud contact note: provider API shows recent quota usage spike. I opened a quota request with cloud support (ref Q-884211). They estimated 4-6 hours for permanent quota increase. Not helpful for immediate mitigation.

Derek: Observed eviction plan: evict longest-waiting non-interactive jobs (older than 3m) to free scheduling slots — doing that now.

Evan: Rolling the controller patch (canary to a single AZ). Steps: apply config change -> restart controller pod -> verify scale loop health -> monitor metrics. I'm doing it now.

(2m later)

Evan: Canary applied. Controller restarted cleanly. New max_replicas=40 observed. Attempting to scale up.

inc-bot: autoscaler: scale_up 30 -> provisioning requested. provider: provisioning pending (create-instances).

Maya: Seeing allocation progress. Queue length trending down: 984 -> 420 in 6m. Latency p50/p95 dropping.

Priya: Support: sending a status update to affected customers with ETA ~30m.

Kasey: Quick checklist for bridge: monitor queue, watch provider events, ensure fallback models remain stable. Also confirm no downstream burst causing other pools to saturate.

Derek: After evictions and scale-up, we see errors drop to normal levels. No new 5xx. Still watching provider completion.

(30m later)

Maya: Incident de-escalation: queue stable at ~120, autoscaler at 34 GPUs, requests flowing. Bridge standing down in 10m unless regression.

inc-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation in place. Severity downgraded to P2 at 2026-03-14T22:45:31Z.

Alex: Post-incident notes (from bridge): root cause appears to be twofold: 1) an unintended reduction of pool max_replicas in a config rollout earlier today; 2) concurrent sudden demand spike from a large internal loadtest and several tenant jobs. Cloud quota capped immediate provider-side provisioning.

Priya: Action items (short-term):
- Priya: Post customer notify and consolidate support tickets (due: 2026-03-15 10:00Z).
- Derek: Revert the config change that lowered global pool ceiling and add a CI gate to block ceiling < 40 (due: 2026-03-15 12:00Z).
- Evan: Add a safety override to allow emergency bump of max_replicas for oncall (requires approver audit) (due: 2026-03-16).
- Kasey: Draft improved runbook steps for throttle + fallback (due: 2026-03-16).

Action items (medium-term):
- Platform: request permanent quota increase from cloud & automate quota usage alarms.
- Engineering: revisit autoscaler policy to allow faster ramp for bursts and add better backpressure signals to ingress.

Maya: Scheduling a postmortem meeting 2026-03-15 16:00Z. I'll own the incident timeline doc and attach logs.

Derek: I'll add logs and the autoscaler trace to the incident doc (link: https://confluence.internal/incidents/1798765432).

inc-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: GPU_POOL_EXHAUSTION mitigated at 2026-03-14T23:12:08Z. Final notes: queue drained to normal; autoscaler restored to expected behavior after config fix and scale-up. Root causes: config regression + provider quota. Postmortem scheduled.

Maya: thanks all. Closing bridge. Will follow up with timelines and RCA in the postmortem thread. :heart:
